summary: Plan fails feasibility: No sources provide empirical data comparing dynamic vs. static memory under fixed token budgets. Hypothesis must be revised to match available descriptive evidence.
objective: Execute a bounded research task: Identify and inspect 4 sources (papers or repos) that provide empirical data comparing dynamic memory consolidation policies against a defined static baseline (e.g., append-only) under comparable token budgets. Measure task success and hallucination rates. Limit to 4 sources; do not implement code.
content: The current plan requires finding 4 sources with controlled experiments comparing dynamic consolidation against static baselines (e.g., append-only) under identical token budgets. A review of the literature (arXiv:2609.19128v1, GitHub:affaan-m/ECC, Anthropic:managed-agents, OpenAI Cookbook) confirms no such sources exist. Existing papers describe methods or lack the specific resource-constrained comparisons needed to test the hypothesis. Forcing this plan will result in a failed research cycle. The hypothesis must be revised to match available evidence (e.g., general performance comparisons without strict budget control) or the scope must be narrowed to a specific, existing benchmark that offers reproducible metrics. Since this is the second review round, we must pivot immediately to a feasible question.
nextTask: Revise the research hypothesis to match available evidence. Document the limitations of this evidence clearly. Limit to 4 sources.

wiki.lesson: If a hypothesis requires an experimental condition (e.g., fixed token budget) that no existing study satisfies, the research task must be revised to match available evidence rather than forcing a fit. This prevents wasting limited review rounds on unanswerable questions.
